structured_output.steelman: Learners who have no natural place to post a code never share; give them one tap that hands the link to whatever channel they already use, a one-line reason to do it, a visible record that it is working, and put it in front of them at the two moments they feel proud enough to send it. Everything else about referrals stays as it is.

ambiguities.text: "One-tap way to send it" is not defined. Native share sheet (Web Share API, absent on most desktop browsers), copy-to-clipboard, or a channel picker are three different builds with three different fallbacks.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The engineer picks one on the first day; if it is copy-link on desktop and share-sheet on mobile, the 'share tap' metric counts two different acts and design has not seen the fallback state.

ambiguities.text: Toast trigger rules are unstated: 'course grade posted' vs the platform's 'grade posted' event (which fires per assignment, weekly, across two courses); no cap, no once-per-event rule, no dismissal memory.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Built literally, a learner gets a referral toast every Friday per course for 8 weeks. The engineer will invent a cap or a dedupe key and it will be wrong for the metric.

ambiguities.text: Toast delivery is unstated: on next dashboard load after the event, or pushed into a live session? Grade posting happens while the learner is in Canvas, not on the dashboard.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: On-load needs a 'pending toast' flag per event; live needs a client event channel the shell may not have. Different size, different backend, and the spec claims no new backend.

ambiguities.text: Referral-state line with N referrals: full list, latest only, or aggregate counts (3 invited / 1 started / 1 credited, £X)? Card height on variant B is fixed by position.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: A learner with twelve invites breaks the card layout; the engineer will truncate or scroll on their own.

ambiguities.text: Source of the amounts in the exchange line ('what the friend gets, what you get'). Amounts are per market and set by finance; incentive amounts are out of scope, but the copy must render them.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: If the referral service does not return the market's amounts, the engineer hardcodes or adds a config read — and the card shows a stale number in a market finance changed.

ambiguities.text: 'When' in the exchange line and 'started' in the state line: does 'start' mean enrolment, first course day, or first paid instalment? The platform says credit lands 'when the referred learner starts' without defining it.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Copy says 'when they start' while the state line flips to 'started' at a different moment; support tickets follow.

ambiguities.text: 'WHEN a referral changes state, show it' — read on dashboard load, or reflect live? Platform events available today do not include referral-state-changed or wallet-credited; the Dependencies section asserts the latter is observable without evidence.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Read-on-load satisfies the AC and is cheap; the engineer will do that and the assertion in Dependencies stays unverified. Confirm which is meant so the claim is either used or deleted.

ambiguities.text: Where the share-tap event and the link's UTM land. 'Measured in-sprint' puts instrumentation in scope, but no analytics sink or landing page is named.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The engineer emits a tap event to whatever exists; if nothing consumes UTM on the landing page, the goal cannot be measured and no one notices until sprint review.

ambiguities.text: Currency and number formatting for the credited amount across markets.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Minor; engineer defaults to the learner's market currency. Confirm that is the wallet's currency.

untestable_criteria.criterion: Goal: share taps per active learner per month; referred starts per 100 active learners. Measured in-sprint.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: Baseline share taps and referred starts for the trailing 30 days before release are recorded; after two weeks live, share taps per active learner in eligible markets ≥ [target] and referred starts per 100 active learners ≥ [target]; both read from the named analytics sink.

untestable_criteria.criterion: THE SYSTEM SHALL state, in one line above the action, what the friend gets, what the learner gets, where it lands (the wallet) and when.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: The exchange line renders the learner's market friend-amount and learner-amount from [named source], the word 'wallet', and the trigger phrase [defined 'start'], and does not wrap at 360px viewport width in the dashboard card or the toast.

hidden_dependencies.name: Finance market/amount configuration
hidden_dependencies.why: The exchange line and the credited-amount line need the per-market amounts finance owns. The spec puts amounts out of scope but cannot render without reading them from somewhere; if the referral service does not expose them, this is a new read.

hidden_dependencies.name: Client-side event delivery for the toast
hidden_dependencies.why: Grade-posted and credential-earned drive the deadline rail, which is rendered from stored state. A toast 'at' the event needs either a pending-toast marker per event or a live channel to the session. Neither is named; the size claim of 'no new backend' rests on it.

hidden_dependencies.name: Analytics sink and referral landing page (UTM)
hidden_dependencies.why: 'Measured from the link's UTM' assumes a landing page that captures UTM and a pipeline the team can query in-sprint. Neither is in the platform context.

hidden_dependencies.name: Referral-state / wallet-credit event
hidden_dependencies.why: Dependencies asserts the wallet credit event is observable to the dashboard; the platform's event list does not include it. Not needed if state is read on load, but the spec should stop claiming it or engineering should confirm it.

size.risk: Toast delivery. If grade-posted and credential-earned are not pushed to the learner's session, the toast needs a pending-notification store keyed per event with dismissal memory — that is new backend and moves this to L. If they are, and the referral service already returns market amounts, it drops back to S.

refinement_agenda: Decide what the primary tap does on mobile and on desktop (share sheet vs copy-link), what the fallback looks like, and where the tap event and the UTM are recorded — so 'share tap' means one thing in the metric.

Decide the toast rules: which events (course final grade only, or every assignment grade), one toast per event or a cap per week, delivery on next dashboard load vs live, and whether dismissal is remembered.
Decide the single source for market amounts and the definition of 'started' so the exchange line and the state line read the same config and flip at the same moment.
structured_output.requester_message:
@jose — this is close, but four things would make an engineer guess on day one, and the size claim of S depends on one of them.

What is owed from you, before triage:
1. Toast rules. The platform's grade-posted event fires per assignment, weekly, per course. Say whether the toast is for the course final grade only or every grade, how many a learner can see in a week, and whether a dismissed toast stays dismissed.
2. Where the amounts come from. Incentive amounts are out of scope, but the card prints them. Tell us whether the referral service returns the market's friend/learner amounts or whether finance holds them somewhere we have to read.
3. Define 'start'. The copy says credit lands 'when they start' and the state line flips to 'started'. Enrolment, first course day, or first paid instalment — pick one.

Owed from design: what the primary tap does on desktop where there is no share sheet, and how the state line behaves with ten referrals on a fixed-height card.

Owed from engineering: whether grade-posted and credential-earned can reach a live session, or whether the toast is shown on next dashboard load. That answer sets the size — S if events are already reachable and amounts come from the service, M otherwise, L if we need a pending-notification store.

Triage is Thursday; today's is under way, so the next one this can enter with answers is 10 September. The current sprint is committed. If this jumps the queue at that triage, the lowest item in Ready slips a sprint — come with the name of what you would trade, and it goes on the agenda with the three decisions above.
